skill.name: documentation-generator
skill.description: Generate code comments, docstrings, README outlines, and API documentation from source code and project context.
skill.summary: Creates consistent developer documentation for code, APIs, and project READMEs.
skill.author: CuriousLearner

content.value_statement: Manual documentation updates are slow and often inconsistent with code behavior. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to draft docstrings, README sections, and API references from source context.
actual_capabilities: Drafts JSDoc comments for JavaScript and TypeScript functions.
Drafts Google-style Python docstrings with arguments, returns, raises, and examples.
Outlines README sections for installation, usage, API reference, configuration, contribution, and license details.
Adapts documentation format for Rust, Java, Go, Python, JavaScript, and TypeScript.
Highlights parameters, return values, exceptions, side effects, edge cases, and performance notes.
limitations: Requires source code or project context to produce accurate documentation.
Does not verify runtime behavior unless paired with tests or execution results.
May need review for domain-specific terms, compliance wording, and public API guarantees.
Does not automatically publish or host generated documentation.

use_cases.title: Document a Utility Module
use_cases.description: Create consistent comments for functions, parameters, returns, exceptions, and examples before code review.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Project README
use_cases.description: Draft core README sections so contributors can install, use, configure, and extend the project.

use_cases.title: Standardize API References
use_cases.description: Convert source structure into predictable API reference sections for SDKs, services, or packages.

prompt_templates.title: Add Basic Docstrings
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the selected functions and draft concise docstrings that explain purpose, parameters, returns, and errors. Keep the existing style.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner documentation for a small file

prompt_templates.title: Generate README Sections
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the project files I provide to draft a README with overview, installation, usage, configuration, API reference, contributing, and license sections.

prompt_templates.title: Match Existing Documentation Style
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the current documentation style in this repository. Update only missing documentation and preserve custom wording in existing comments.

prompt_templates.title: Create API Reference From Source
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a structured API reference from these modules. Include public classes, methods, parameters, return values, exceptions, side effects, and realistic examples.

output_examples.input: A TypeScript utility function with price, tax, and discount parameters.
output: Parameter notes for base price, tax rate, and optional discount.
Return and error descriptions plus a small usage example.

output_examples.input: A Python service class with public methods and raised exceptions.
output: A class summary that states the main responsibility.
Method documentation with arguments, return values, and exceptions.
Notes about side effects and expected caller behavior.

output_examples.input: A repository that needs a first README.
output: A project overview for new users.
Installation, usage, configuration, API, contribution, and license sections.
Placeholder guidance for details the maintainer must verify.

best_practices: Provide representative source files and any existing documentation style before asking for updates.
Review generated examples for accuracy, especially around errors, side effects, and edge cases.
Keep generated documentation close to the code it describes.
anti_patterns: Asking for full project documentation without sharing source files or API context.
Replacing carefully written custom documentation without checking intent.
Publishing generated docs without verifying examples and installation steps.

faq.question: What languages does this skill support?
faq.answer: It gives patterns for JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Rust, Java, and Go documentation.

faq.question: Can it generate a full README?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft overview, installation, usage, API, configuration, contribution, and license sections from project context.

faq.question: Does it edit files automatically?
faq.answer: It provides documentation guidance. File edits depend on how the host agent is asked to apply the output.

faq.question: Can it follow existing documentation style?
faq.answer: Yes. It instructs the agent to match existing project conventions and update only missing documentation.

faq.question: Will it guarantee technical accuracy?
faq.answer: No. Generated docs should be reviewed against tests, implementation details, and product requirements.

faq.question: Is network access required?
faq.answer: No. The skill text does not require network access or external services.
